system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review (Buyer Side)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. Several items would also remove protections the playbook treats as non-negotiable, including the fraud carve-out, the Fundamental/Title regime, and completion-day certainty on Bluefen and Riverlark. I recommend rejecting the package as drafted and marking up against our positions.

## Process point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the efficiency note

The Seller asks us to treat [STANDARD] clauses as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to focus only on [OPEN] items. I don't recommend accepting that approach:

- Nothing in the package shows our authority process cleared any of these positions. Playbook sec 0.4/6.3 says counterparty labels such as "agreed", "negotiated", "settled", "fair and balanced" or "pre-cleared" are not firm instructions or clearance.
- Every [STANDARD] item in this package departs from our playbook. Skipping them would mean accepting them.
- The Seller is also wrong that the parties "have already accepted" the disclosure and limitation package. The 20% cap and the 18-month period are our conditional fallbacks, and neither has written authority from Amelia Frost.

We should review all clauses in full.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% is a fallback that needs Frost's written authority | Reject. Hold 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer the fallback without authority |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Frost's written approval | Reject. Hold 24 months |
| Blanket limitation application | Any limit applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Fundamental/Title and fraud are separate regimes | Reject. Limits apply only to general warranty claims |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. Restore separate regime |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these, to the maximum extent enforceable | Reject. Add the fraud carve-out, which no one may waive |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, public registers, Accounts | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Reject. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for matters the Buyer or advisers knew of or could find in data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject and delete |
| Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient | Reject. Make effective consent a completion condition with evidence |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Release provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Reject. Require payout from Completion funds |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | DD-005 AUD 420,000 not itemised | Must be a specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs | Reject silent exclusion. Require itemisation or seller funding and address on-costs |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure | Reject. Broaden the indemnity |
| Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6, Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction | Do not accept "immaterial". Require the preservation and investigation steps |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course" | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept the characterisation. Assess the renewals; no automatic deduction |
| Tax/IP | "Settled" under the general regime | Remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | Reject "settled". Keep Tax and IP separate and open |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register as evidence of title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof | Require independent evidence (see below) |
| Non-admission (DL 1.4) | No admission that any consent, payment or notice is "legally required" | Our contractual conditions stand regardless of the Seller's view | Reject any reading that the non-admission removes our consent or payout conditions |

## Reasoning on the material issues

**1. Stacked exclusions.** Under the Seller's package, the whole data room is disclosed (DL 1.1), public records count (DL 1.2 and cl 8.3), and buyer knowledge bars claims for anything discoverable there. Together these would bar claims on most of the diligence findings in this letter, including Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident and title. This is the single most important point to reject.

**2. Fraud and Fundamental/Title override.** The "any Claims of any nature" wording and the blanket limitation override would catch fraud and title. The playbook says both are carved out and cannot be waived.

**3. Completion certainty.** The Bluefen consent is worth about AUD 3.6m of revenue (around 30%). Riverlark has about AUD 3.2m outstanding. The disclosure confirms neither is resolved (DL 2 and 3). Treating consent as satisfied on delivery, or deferring the release, leaves us paying for risk we have not priced.

**4. Funds flow.** The Seller says the funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics", but DL 5 confirms the AUD 420,000 bonuses are not in it. Silent exclusion would shift cost to the Buyer. The on-cost question is also unanswered.

**5. Ironquay.** DL 4 confirms the SOW3 transfer depends on payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 open amount comes from DD-010 and is not verified as either owed or paid. The narrow indemnity leaves IP transfer risk with us. We should neither assume the amount is owed nor concede it is not.

**6. Incident.** The disclosure says the facts are not established. The Seller's "not material" view is an assertion, not a finding. The records (about 1,240 names, business emails, roles and timestamps) may raise privacy questions, so we should get Australian privacy advice on whether any notification assessment applies. We should not assert a breach or a notification duty ourselves.

**7. Title.** The share register is the Seller's own document. We need independent evidence.

## Facts to refresh and open items

- The data room snapshot is as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks old. Refresh the bonus, Riverlark, Bluefen, Ironquay and incident facts before mark-up.
- **Office lease (DL 7):** the notification obligation is identified, but the landlord consent question is not resolved. Get the clause and confirm whether any consent is required for the share sale.
- **Mossvale (DL 9):** the assignment restriction is identified, but it is not confirmed whether the share sale triggers it. Get the clause and confirm.
- **Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011):** check whether the three renewals overlap or double-count, and whether each is terminable or accrued.
- **Title evidence:** request independent evidence such as a current ASIC company extract, PPSR search, and confirmation of signing authority. Verify the register rather than relying on DD-012.
- **Frost authority:** confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback has been approved. Do not offer the 20% cap or 18 months without written authority.

## Recommendations summary

1. **Reject the efficiency note.** Review every clause. Do not treat any Seller-labelled [STANDARD] item as cleared.
2. **Hold our core commercial positions:** 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24-month general period.
3. **Restore the Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Add the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, non-waivable.
5. **Reject whole-data-room and public-register disclosure.** Require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Delete the buyer-knowledge exclusion** in cl 8.3, or restrict any qualifier to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and never against title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Make Bluefen a completion condition:** effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
8. **Require the Riverlark payout from Completion funds**, with effective security releases. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
9. **Itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses** (plus on-costs) as a funds flow line item, or require Seller funding.
10. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** and keep the SOW3 cure. Verify the AUD 180,000 position.
11. **Incident:** require log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Take privacy advice. Accept no "immaterial" characterisation.
12. **Sandbar:** assess the renewals. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Keep Tax and IP open** and separate from the general regime.
14. **Title:** require independent ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence.
15. **Reject any use of the DL 1.4 non-admission** to override our contractual consent or payout conditions.

Before the mark-up goes out, the deal team should confirm the facts above with current sources and have qualified NSW counsel review the final drafting.
=== END ADVICE ===
